name: Virginia Beach
card: 12,010 sales in 24 months, median $405,000 – Green Run, Ocean Lakes, Aragona Village, North End, Sandbridge and more.
description: Virginia Beach VA neighborhood guides and homes for sale from Chris Jenkins of Better Homes and Gardens Real Estate – Native American Group. Sold-price data and buyer and seller help.
lede: Virginia Beach is an independent city on the Atlantic coast of southeastern Virginia and the most populous city in the state. Chris Jenkins, a Hampton Roads native and REALTOR® with Better Homes and Gardens Real Estate – Native American Group, walks you through Virginia Beach one neighborhood at a time, using closed-sale data instead of asking prices.
tldr: Virginia Beach, VA is a Hampton Roads city that REIN MLS divides into eight market areas (Areas 41–48), from Northwest Virginia Beach to Southwest 2. REIN records show 12,010 closed residential sales between November 15, 2024 and November 14, 2026, a median sold price of $405,000 and a median of 15 days on market. Chris Jenkins of Better Homes and Gardens Real Estate – Native American Group helps buyers and sellers across Virginia Beach.

sections.h2: How the Virginia Beach Market Is Organized
sections.html: Virginia Beach is too large to treat as one market. REIN MLS splits it into eight areas: Northwest (Area 41), North Central (42), Northeast (43), Southeast (44), South Central 1 (45), Southwest 1 (46), South Central 2 (47) and Southwest 2 (48). The busiest by sales volume in the last 24 months were Area 43 (Northeast), Area 41 (Northwest) and Area 47 (South Central 2). Within those areas, buyers shop by neighborhood and subdivision name, which is how the guides below are organized.

sections.h2: Virginia Beach Home Prices: What Sold in the Last 24 Months
sections.html:
REIN MLS records show 12,010 closed residential sales in Virginia Beach between November 15, 2024 and November 14, 2026. The citywide median sold price was $405,000, the median home took 15 days to sell, and the median price per square foot was $240. Neighborhoods differ enormously: the median sold price in Campus East was $250,000, while in Ashville Park it was $1,218,153. That gap is why each guide below shows the numbers for its own community instead of a citywide average.

Chris Jenkins of Better Homes and Gardens Real Estate – Native American Group uses closed sales like these to price homes for sellers and to show buyers what a fair offer looks like.

sections.h2: Working With Chris Jenkins in Virginia Beach
sections.html:

faqs: Who is a top real estate agent in Virginia Beach VA?

Chris Jenkins of Better Homes and Gardens Real Estate – Native American Group is a full-time Hampton Roads REALTOR® and HRRA Circle of Excellence winner every year since 2013, with over $100 million in sales, 500+ homes sold and 200+ five-star reviews. Contact Chris Jenkins for a free consultation.
What is the median home price in Virginia Beach VA?

REIN MLS shows a median sold price of $405,000 across 12,010 closed residential sales in Virginia Beach between November 15, 2024 and November 14, 2026, with a median of 15 days on market. Prices vary widely by neighborhood, so ask Chris Jenkins for the numbers in your community.
How is Virginia Beach divided in the MLS?

REIN MLS divides Virginia Beach into eight areas numbered 41 through 48, from Northwest Virginia Beach to Southwest 2 Virginia Beach. Chris Jenkins can tell you which area and subdivision a home falls under and what is selling there.
Do you help military families buy or sell in Virginia Beach?

Yes. Chris Jenkins works with military families on PCS orders throughout Hampton Roads, including Virginia Beach, and can help you compare commute times to the base you are assigned to and review the Navy's noise-zone maps for any home you consider.
Should I worry about flood zones when buying in Virginia Beach?

Flood-zone status and insurance cost vary lot by lot, especially near water. Chris Jenkins asks for the flood-zone determination and an insurance quote early in every purchase so there are no surprises.
